function: Unsupervised DNNs jointly choose D2D transmit power, cellular channel allocation and discrete RIS phase shifts to maximize D2D energy efficiency in a UAV-served network (pp. 3, 7-8).
system: Single-antenna UAV aerial BS, CUEs and D2D pairs; passive reflecting RIS, M=4 elements, 3-bit phases (L=8), amplitude 1; frequency band not stated (pp. 4, 11).
method: Fully connected DNNs (power, channel, RIS modules with softmax outputs, optional dropout) trained offline, unsupervised with penalty loss and Adam; centralized and distributed variants (pp. 3, 8-10).
data_channel: Simulated CSI: Rician for RIS links, Rayleigh with path loss for the others; 10^4 training and 10^3 testing samples (pp. 4-5, 12).
test_conditions: Default UAV at 30 m, K=2, D=3, M=4; test sweeps over M (4-64) and UAV altitude (30-380 m); training conditions of the sweeps not stated (pp. 11-13).
baselines: Non-learned: exhaustive-search optimum, max-power/random-phase, random-power/random-phase, no RIS. No earlier learned method; only own variants (centralized with/without dropout, distributed) (p. 12).
metrics: Energy efficiency of D2D users (bits/Hz/Joule), training loss and EE versus learning rate, computation time (pp. 12-13).
complexity: Total time to compute Fig. 13 curves on Intel i5-12500 CPU: optimum 314.20 s, centralized DNN 68.18 s, distributed DNN 92.37 s; no operation or parameter counts (p. 13).
q1_support: p. 5: "they follow Rayleigh fading with path loss taken into consideration"; own Rician (RIS links, p. 4) and Rayleigh simulator, no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 13: "To verify the generalization ability of the algorithm, we consider different UAV’s flying altitudes"; the training altitude is never stated (Table II: 10^4 training, 10^3 testing samples), so a held-out test or retraining per altitude is not excluded.
q3_support: p. 12: "we can use exhaustive search to find the optimal solution"; baselines are exhaustive search, random power/phase and no RIS; the only learned schemes are the paper's own variants, so no earlier learned baseline.
q4_support: p. 13: "are 314.20, 68.18, and 92.37, respectively" (seconds to compute and plot the Fig. 13 curves for the optimum, centralized DNN and distributed DNN); measured runtime only.
q5_support: p. 11: "empirical channel models are exploited to train the DNNs"; channels come from the authors' own simulator, with no code or data link, no public dataset and no availability statement.
notes: Title and DOI on p. 1 match. Area 6 by the specificity order (aerial UAV BS, learned power and channel resource control plus RIS phases); area 3 (RIS phase shifts) also fits and is the alternative. Single-antenna links but a RIS is present, so the system check passes. q2 is borderline: the altitude sweep is called a generalization test (p. 13) but the training altitude is not stated. q4 rests on a coarse measured total runtime.
